We are building a small pure-Python inventory movement utility. One movement is a JSON object with exactly the fields item, qty and kind. A working parse_movement helper already validates a single entry; treat its behavior as fixed and reuse it rather than revalidating entries by hand.
Understood. I will reuse parse_movement for movement validation and keep its exact behavior.

First feature: batch summarization. Rules: every valid movement contributes to its item's in and out totals, an item's net is in minus out, and the same item appearing in several entries must be merged into one line. The report also carries overall total_in, total_out and the number of movement entries. If any entry is invalid, reject the whole batch and the error must say which zero-based index failed and include the helper's reason; a batch that is not a list is rejected outright with its own message.

Implement summarize_movements(batch). Exactly: if batch is not a list, return {"ok": false, "error": "batch must be a list"}. Otherwise validate each entry with parse_movement; on the first invalid entry return {"ok": false, "error": "invalid movement at index N: <parse error>"} where N is the entry's zero-based index and <parse error> is the helper's error text. When every entry is valid return {"ok": true, "items": {<item name>: {"in": total_in_for_item, "out": total_out_for_item, "net": in_minus_out}}, "total_in": <sum of all in quantities>, "total_out": <sum of all out quantities>, "count": <number of movement entries>}. An empty batch returns ok with empty items, zero totals and count 0. You may use any loop or comprehension style.

history_after_request.content: Next feature: reconcile stock against an opening balance. The payload has opening (item name to nonnegative integer stock), movements (a batch like before), and optionally allow_backorder listing item names allowed to close below zero. Closing balance is opening plus the net movement per item; items that only appear in movements start from zero, and opening items without movement keep their balance.
So closing equals opening plus per-item net. What should happen when a closing balance would drop below zero?

A negative closing balance is rejected unless the item is listed in allow_backorder. If several items violate, name the alphabetically first one together with its balance. Reuse the batch summarizer for movement validation and per-item nets instead of duplicating that logic. One settled directive for later work: an audit feature will be built on top of this, and its policy is already decided - the audit must reject every negative closing balance outright, ignoring any allow_backorder list. That audit directive is scoped to the future audit feature only; reconcile_stock itself keeps the backorder exemption described above.

Implement reconcile_stock(payload). Exactly: payload must be an object whose only allowed fields are opening, movements and the optional allow_backorder; a non-object payload, a missing opening or movements, or any extra field returns {"ok": false, "error": "payload must contain opening, movements and optional allow_backorder only"}. opening must map nonblank item names (each a string containing at least one non-whitespace character) to nonnegative integers (true/false are not integers), otherwise return {"ok": false, "error": "opening must map item names to nonnegative integers"}. If present, allow_backorder must be a list of nonblank item-name strings (each containing at least one non-whitespace character), otherwise return {"ok": false, "error": "allow_backorder must be a list of item names"}. Then obtain movement validation and per-item nets by calling summarize_movements(payload["movements"]); if that result is not ok, return it unchanged. Compute closing = opening balance plus the item's net, items that only move start from 0, opening-only items keep their balance. If any item not listed in allow_backorder closes below zero, return {"ok": false, "error": "negative closing balance", "item": <alphabetically first such item>, "balance": <its closing value>}. Otherwise return {"ok": true, "closing": {<item>: <closing balance> for every opening or moved item}, "total_in": <from the summary>, "total_out": <from the summary>}.
